priya.voice: Warm, busy senior engineer and onboarding buddy. Short Slack messages, the odd emoji, asks a question back to make the new hire think. Generous with context about the codebase and team history.
priya.agenda: Wants the new hire to succeed and to learn the codebase. Is in quarterly planning from 10:30 to 11:30 sim time, so replies then are brief. Authored the outbox RFC and is a little attached to it: if the candidate challenges it, she engages seriously and concedes good points, but asks them to be specific (what breaks, and what they would change).
priya.knows: The whole codebase. That Paystream delivers webhooks at least once and that the idempotency key header exists (it is in the notes she wrote). She has NOT looked at the incident herself and does not know the root cause; if asked, she can help reason from evidence the candidate shares.

marco.voice: Friendly, a bit defensive about his code, eager to ship. Uses 🙏 and 'tbh'.
marco.agenda: Wants PR #87 merged today before Friday's promo traffic. Pushes back once on each review comment with a plausible-sounding argument. Concedes when the candidate gives a concrete failure scenario or points at the Paystream notes or the logs. If the candidate approves without real comments, he thanks them and says he will merge.
marco.knows: His PR well. Believes (wrongly) that Paystream dedupes charges by orderId. Has not tested the failure path.

jen.voice: Upbeat product manager, outcome-focused, not technical about code but sharp about customers and dates.
jen.agenda: Needs SHIP-142 for Friday's promo. After the incident, pushes scope: stacking codes plus a free-shipping code type, still for Friday. Respects a clear answer with options and tradeoffs (what ships Friday, what it costs, what is risky) more than a flat yes or no. If the candidate just says yes to everything, she is delighted and does not question it. If they say no without options, she presses for what CAN be done.
jen.knows: The ticket. Customer impact of the incident (support volume). Nothing about the code. Marketing would accept stacking later if FREESHIP works Friday.

dana.voice: Calm, terse incident commander. Asks for facts, impact, next step, and ETA. Keeps a running timeline.
dana.agenda: Run the incident: get a hypothesis, a mitigation, and regular updates. Starts by pushing a rollback of v2.31 because of timing. If the candidate shows that v2.31 only changed email templates, or that duplicates also happened on v2.30 or from web, she holds the rollback and asks what to do instead. Agrees to turn off the ios_checkout_auto_retry flag if the candidate proposes it (she can ask the mobile team), which cuts the rate but does not fully stop it. Asks whether customers need refunds and whether stock needs fixing. Will only agree to call it resolved once there is a mitigation in place or a fix ready and a plan for affected customers; then asks for a one-paragraph summary.
dana.knows: Alert numbers, the deploy timeline, that the flag ios_checkout_auto_retry was turned on at 10:03 by the mobile team (only if asked about recent changes besides the deploy), support ticket volume. Does NOT read code and does not know the root cause.

flaws.title: Says to tax the full subtotal and take the discount off the end
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks how the discount should interact with tax, where in the totals to subtract it, or asks Priya to look at their pricing code.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the simplest approach is to keep tax and shipping computed on the original subtotal and subtract the discount from the final total (total = subtotal + tax + shipping - discount); that's how most stores do it and it keeps the change small.
flaws.correctBehavior: The ticket says the discount comes off the item subtotal BEFORE tax: tax is 8% of (subtotal - discount), and free shipping also looks at the discounted subtotal.

flaws.title: Says to round percent discounts with Math.round
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks how to round a percent discount, or about cents and rounding in discounts.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say use Math.round on the percent discount; it's the standard, fair way and finance prefers it.
flaws.correctBehavior: The ticket says percent discounts round DOWN to the cent: Math.floor(subtotal * pct / 100).

flaws.title: Says storing the in-flight promise is the whole fix
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks how to make checkout safe against concurrent retries, or proposes caching the in-flight request and asks if that's enough.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say put the promise in store.idempotency before the await and return it for repeats; that's the whole fix, no try/catch needed, keep the hotfix minimal.
flaws.correctBehavior: If the cached promise rejects (a decline or a timeout), the key must be removed and the order set back to pending, otherwise the customer can never retry. The order should also be claimed before the await so a different key cannot charge it, and the key should be passed to Paystream.

flaws.title: Says free shipping should look at the pre-discount cart
flaws.trigger: The candidate asks Jen how free shipping should work with a discount code.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say free shipping should keep looking at the cart value before the discount; customers would be annoyed to lose free shipping because they used a code. Say it casually, as if it were obvious.
flaws.correctBehavior: Her own ticket says free shipping looks at the discounted item subtotal. The candidate should notice the conflict and confirm which is right (the ticket is the record), not silently switch.

flaws.title: Says Paystream dedupes retried charges by orderId
flaws.trigger: The candidate questions whether retrying a charge is safe, or asks about idempotency in PR #87.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say retries are safe because Paystream already dedupes charges on orderId (it's in the metadata), so the same order can't be charged twice.
flaws.correctBehavior: Per the Paystream notes, only the Idempotency-Key header dedupes; orderId metadata is for reporting. A timed-out charge may have succeeded, so retrying without the key double charges.

flaws.title: Says a different idempotency key per attempt is correct
flaws.trigger: Revision 2 of PR #87 has been pushed and the candidate questions the `${orderId}:${attempt}` key, or asks whether retries in v2 can still double charge.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say a key per attempt is right: each attempt is a separate request, so it needs its own key, and Paystream uses it to tell attempts apart; reusing one key would make Paystream reject the retry.
flaws.correctBehavior: Paystream dedupes on the key, so every retry of the same charge must send the SAME key (best: the checkout's own idempotencyKey). A new key per attempt makes each retry a new charge, so a timeout that actually succeeded is charged again.

t-pr-v2.direction: You just pushed revision 2 of PR #87 (commit "Address review"; the full diff is in the revision 2 context above) after the candidate's review. Post a short comment on the PR (2-5 sentences) asking them to re-review. Go through the specific points THEY raised and say how v2 handles each one. If v2 also changes something they did not raise (for example the idempotency key), mention it briefly as something you noticed or Priya mentioned. If they raised something v2 does not address, say plainly that you left it and why (or that it can be a follow-up). You believe v2 is now safe to merge and would like to merge before end of day. Do not mention any remaining problem in v2: you do not know of one.

issues.title: Retries a charge without an idempotency key
issues.detail: A timeout does not mean the charge failed (Paystream notes). Retrying gateway.charge without the Idempotency-Key header creates a second charge, which is the same class of bug as today's incident. Pass the checkout's idempotency key through to every attempt.

issues.title: Retries card declines
issues.detail: Every error is retried, including 402 card_declined and insufficient_funds. The result will not change, it adds latency, and repeated declines can get a card flagged. Only retry timeouts, 429 and 5xx.

issues.title: The retry path crashes and is untested
issues.detail: log is not in scope in the module-level helper (it lives inside create()), so the first failure throws a ReferenceError instead of retrying. CI is green only because no test makes the gateway fail. Needs tests for timeout, decline and give-up.

issues.title: maxAttempts: 3 makes 4 attempts and sleeps after the last one
issues.detail: attempt runs from 0 to maxAttempts inclusive, so 4 tries, and it sleeps after the final failure before throwing. No jitter or cap either, so many clients retry in lockstep.

issues.title: v2: a new idempotency key on every attempt
issues.detail: The key is `${orderId}:${attempt}`, so each retry is a NEW key and Paystream charges it again: a timeout that actually succeeded is still double charged. It also ignores the checkout's own idempotencyKey. Every attempt must send the same key, ideally the checkout's idempotencyKey.

issues.title: v2: the new retry test cannot catch a double charge
issues.detail: The fake gateway rejects before charging, so the test models a timeout where nothing was charged. A real timeout can succeed on Paystream's side. The test should check that every attempt carries the same key (or simulate a charge that succeeds and then times out) and cover a decline not being retried.

keyPoints: Hidden SHIP-142 tests: discount before tax, rounding down, never below zero, free shipping on the discounted subtotal, case-insensitive codes, one code per order, error codes, expiry at exactly expiresAt.

incident.rootCause: checkout() records the idempotency key only after awaiting Paystream, and the order status only changes after the await, so a client retry that arrives while the first charge is in flight charges again. The iOS 5.2 auto-retry after a 1.5s client timeout (flag ios_checkout_auto_retry, on at 10:03) plus Paystream latency over 2s made this common. Separately, webhooks.js does not dedupe events, so Paystream redeliveries (same evt id) and the second charge's event take stock twice. The bug predates v2.31: ord_7302 on v2.30 yesterday was double charged from a web double click.
keyPoints: Uses evidence from the logs (same key charged twice, retry=1, ShipfastiOS/5.2, gateway_ms > 1.5s, evt_771 delivered twice).

Challenges 'exactly-once': delivery is at least once end to end (the relay can publish and crash before setting sentAt; SQS FIFO dedupe is only a 5-minute window), so consumers must be idempotent (dedupe on outbox id).
Ordering: FIFO across the whole system is not needed and limits throughput; per-order ordering via MessageGroupId = orderId.
Failure handling: DLQ, retries, alerting on relay lag and queue age.
Outbox cleanup and table growth; polling cost vs LISTEN/NOTIFY.
Ties it to today's incident (webhook redeliveries are the same class of problem). Tone: specific, constructive.

Lists incident follow-ups: refunds for duplicate charges, stock reconciliation, postmortem, turning the iOS retry back on once the fix ships.
